findings.summary: Merge commits in the PR range would be flagged wrongly
findings.evidence: classify_commit (land.rs:168) uses Change::of_commit, which diffs against the first parent. If a PR merges main into itself (GitHub 'Update branch'), that diff contains main's governed changes, so the merge commit would be reported as 'changes governed content' even though main already covers that content. Fix: Choose and document what happens to merge commits in merge_base..head. Either skip a merge whose tree has no governed change against the merged-in main parent, or state that PRs must be rebased and add a test for it. Do not leave this behavior unspecified.
findings.location: Risks: 'classify merge commits against the first parent as land.rs does'

findings.summary: Criterion 3's test could pass for the wrong reason
findings.evidence: This criterion guards against a regression, but its 'fails without' line is hypothetical ('records-only or verified-looking'). The hand commit is not said to be records-only, so a version that sent main's commits to the pre-merge rule could still flag it as governed content, and the test would pass for the wrong reason. Fix: Make the unattributed commit on main records-only or an intervention, which the pre-merge rule would accept. Assert the attribution wording 'no landing record names it', so the test fails if main's commits go through the pre-merge rule.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 3, 'Fails without the behavior'

findings.summary: PR violations would carry the wrong hint
findings.evidence: history.rs:84 gives every JobRecords finding the hint 'land the change through athena land --pr so a landing record names it, or run athena status…'. For a PR commit that is uncovered under the pre-merge rule, that advice is wrong. Fix: Give pre-merge violations their own hint: land a verified job or declare an intervention.

findings.summary: The CI fetch change can be smaller
findings.evidence: checkout with fetch-depth 0 already brings refs/remotes/origin/* (main and athena/records), which is why PR #175 reached the attribution rule even though the records fetch is skipped on PRs. Fetching on every event is harmless. The comment at ci.yml:102-103 is the part that really needs rewriting. Fix: Keep the change small. Remove the `if:` on the records fetch, rewrite the comment, and note that origin/main comes from the full-depth checkout or is fetched explicitly.

summary: The plan fixes the fault where it starts. check_after_cutover (history.rs:68-106) passes the whole tip to legacy::check_attribution_with_legacy, and that walk follows main's first-parent line after C0 (attribution.rs:283-295). Passing the merge base as main_tip, and classifying merge_base..head with a classifier moved out of land.rs classify_commit (land.rs:162-214), keeps main's path byte-identical and gives the pre-merge rule one source. I read these functions; they exist with the shapes the plan assumes. Keeping verification_id and the 'lies between' prefix in core respects the crate layering. The demonstrations run the real binary on fixture branches and check pass/fail and the named sha, so they would fail without the change. Four findings, none blocking: merge commits inside the PR range are left unspecified, the main-unchanged test should use a commit the pre-merge rule would accept, PR violations need their own hint, and a CI nit. The work fits one producer run.
